Group rules from the admins
Be Kind and Courteous
We're all in this together to create a welcoming environment. Let's treat everyone with respect. Healthy debates are natural, but kindness is required.
No Hate Speech or Bullying
Make sure everyone feels safe. Bullying of any kind isn't allowed, and degrading comments about things like race, religion, culture, sexual orientation, gender or identity will not be tolerated.
No Promotions or Spam
Give more than you take to this group. Self-promotion, spam and irrelevant links aren't allowed. Adding your website or social media to your posts is okay as long as it doesn't become obtrusive.
Posting
Please post photos sets in an album once per day. Posting many photos can clutter the news feed with very similar content. Exceptions can be made for very different content (i.e. Landscape vs Portait)
Minneapolis Photos and Discussion
Please post primarily Minneapolis photos or topics for discussion. Please be sure the photos are yours or you provide full credit and have permission from the photographer.

Help us give rescue dogs their best chance at finding a home!
I am a volunteer photographer and foster with Rescue Network. We finally got a physical building as the rescue has grown significantly and are setting up a dedicated photography space at our rescue to take beautiful, consistent adoption photos of the dogs/cats.
We're looking for a gently used camera, ideally with a compatible lens, to help us get started. The camera doesn't need to be the newest model or fancy professional equipment, just reliable and capable of taking nice portraits. If we happened to get a Nikon DSLR, I have a lens I can donate to the rescue as I shoot mirrorless now. I wouldn’t be able to take all of the adoption photos as I work as a nurse during the week days, but I help out where I can with my personal camera. There are a couple of other photographers with the rescue and I think the rescue would like to train in some other people. I wish that I could donate my Nikon D7000 or D750 cameras but my D7000 has a very high shutter count and my D750 shutter went out last year and costs $400+ to get fixed.
If you're a photographer who has upgraded your equipment, have a spare camera collecting dust, or know someone who might be willing to donate or sell equipment at a rescue-friendly price, we'd love to hear from you! Or if anyone knows of anyone at shops willing to offer a non profit discount.
I’d be open to sweetening the deal and trading my services also. I have experience with family photoshoots, senior pictures, grad photos, maternity, dog legacy shoots, etc. I’m down for pretty much anything except newborn and weddings
Feel free to comment/message me if you have something that might be a good fit. Thank you in advance

"The Leaves Stood Still"
Even the wind stopped to watch this one.
The sun slipped down into the treetops like it was trying not to wake anyone. The clouds stretched out like they had all the time in the world. The field held its breath. Out by the edge of the woods, a fallen branch just lay there, in no hurry to be anywhere.
That's fall at sunset. The whole world turns down the volume and tucks itself in, one gold leaf at a time. No rush, no noise, just a quiet that feels like a gentle "well done, today."
Side Life community, we're growing toward 10,000 of us who still pause for the sunset. Thanks for pausing with me.
Where do you go when you need the world to go quiet?

Title this photograph for me. Drop it in the comments below.
Some days don't end. They glow.
I almost missed this one. The sun was already sliding into the treeline, the grass had turned to copper, and a tired old truck sat parked where the day's work left off. Nothing staged. Nothing fixed. Just the field exhaling.
Fall does this. It takes ordinary things, like a farm truck, a stand of cedars, and a patch of weeds, and lights them like they matter. Maybe they do. Maybe the end of a long day is the most honest light we get.
Side Life community, we're chasing 10,000 of us who slow down enough to notice moments like this. This one's for you.
What's the last thing that stopped you in your tracks this fall?

Exploring the iconic landmarks of downtown Minneapolis!
Facts about the Grain Belt Beer sign and Hennepin Ave bridge!
The Legendary Grain Belt Beer sign on Nicollet Island was originally built way back in 1941 for just $5,000. Today, it stands as one of the largest remaining neon signs in the entire Midwest.
Hennepin Ave bridge is the exact site of the very first permanent bridge built to span the entire length of the Mississippi River, which originally opened in 1855.

It's been a minute since I got out to chase a sunset. This week, I finally did.
Side Life community, we're building toward 10k together, and this one is a reminder of why I do this. I stepped away from the busy and found this country road at golden hour, just a couple minutes from our new place, along a family farm I'm already falling for.
In post, I let the photograph become art. It isn't perfect or tack sharp, but the texture and motion blur felt just right, like the way a memory feels when you think back on it.
New home, new roads, same love for the light.
Where's the place close to home that makes you slow down?
